establishes: per-clone occupancy and its across-clone variance, with calibrated tests and profile intervals; an explicit identifiability window for the rate
unresolved: over-disperses per-clone rates: reports the largest spurious V_log k of the three binary methods when the true value is zero
unique_contribution: states which rates the tree can resolve, and flags its own boundary cases

establishes: phylogenetic autocorrelation with an analytical z-test; a transition matrix Q whose stationary distribution recovers occupancy
unresolved: rate estimate is nearly flat in the true rate and biased low by 1.6-2.3x; no interval on Q; fails on clones fixed in one state
unique_contribution: the only method here with an analytical significance test for phylogenetic signal itself

establishes: depth-stratified transition matrices, so rates are allowed to change with developmental stage; occupancy recovered as well as the others
unresolved: rate biased high by 11-16x and exactly invariant to branch times; 3-18% of clones return no finite rate; no per-rate interval
unique_contribution: the only method that does not assume a single rate across the tree

establishes: OU parameters for a continuous trait with AICc model selection; theta tracks clone occupancy in most mechanisms
unresolved: theta carries no signal when states are near-frozen; alpha is in units of whatever clock the tree carries, which is unit edges when the tree has none
unique_contribution: the only method that models a continuous phenotype natively, and the only one that selects between evolutionary models

establishes: clone-associated occupancy is a real and recoverable property of lineage-recorded data, and the finding does not depend on which method is used
unresolved: switching kinetics: three implementations disagree by more than an order of magnitude on identical trees, bracketing the truth from both sides
unique_contribution: the disagreement itself is the evidence that the rate is not identified by these data
